title: Overcast Compat Scenario IR
description: One scenario file: compat/model/scenarios/<service>.json, written by cmd/compatgen from a recipe, or compat/model/authored/<group>.json, written by a human. The suite interpreters execute either; the typed suites compile either. The IR is closed: every construct an interpreter must implement is defined here, and README.md in this directory is the normative description. A test cannot be represented without at least one assertion clause.

$comment.description: Prose, for an authored scenario: what it ports, and why the clauses are what they are. Every consumer ignores it. cmd/compatgen never writes one, so a generated file carries none and byte-identical regeneration is unaffected.

service.description: The Overcast capability service key (compat registry `service`).

Client.description: What an interpreter needs to construct a client for this service without a naming table of its own. Per-SDK package names are derived from sdkId (see README § Naming).

sdkId.description: The Smithy aws.api#service sdkId, e.g. "SQS", "Organizations", "Cost Explorer".

endpointPrefix.description: The aws.api#service endpointPrefix; also the aws CLI command name for every service in the pilot.

protocol.description: The wire protocol, spelled as the Smithy protocol trait is (aws.protocols#awsJson1_0 → awsJson1_0).

targetPrefix.description: For AWS JSON protocols, the X-Amz-Target prefix without its trailing dot: the header is `<targetPrefix>.<Operation>`.

awsQueryCompatible.description: The service carries aws.protocols#awsQueryCompatible: it was migrated from Query and still returns the Query error code in the x-amzn-query-error header, as `<code>;<Sender|Receiver>`. When true an interpreter accepts that code as well as the JSON __type/code; when false the JSON body is the only carrier. Always present, so "false" and "not stated" are not confusable.

$comment.description: Prose, for an authored scenario. Ignored by every consumer and never generated.

name.description: The registry group name: <service>-gen-<resource> or <service>-gen-probe for a generated group, the ported group's own name for an authored one.

parallel.description: The group's tests may run concurrently with one another, bounded by the interpreter's own parallel-slot count. Present and true on every probe group and on no lifecycle group: a probe has no setup, no teardown and no exports, so nothing orders its tests, while a lifecycle group's tests hand resources to one another through the context bag. An interpreter that ignores it still runs the group correctly, in order.

setup.description: Calls made before the first test, in order. A failure skips every test in the group and still runs teardown.

teardown.description: Calls made after the last test, in order, each wrapped individually: an error or an unresolvable $ref skips that call and continues.

params.description: Input members, as modeled, each a Value.

export.description: Context paths to set from the response: `"queue.url": "$.QueueUrl"`.

$comment.description: Prose, for an authored scenario. Ignored by every consumer and never generated.

op.description: The operation the test exercises; equals the primary call's op.

assert.description: At least one clause, always. A test with no assertion is not representable.

depends.description: Earlier tests in the group whose exports this test consumes; mirrored into the registry.

Assertion.description: One clause of the closed assertion set. `kind` selects which other fields are present.

assert.description: The retried clause: readback, listContains or absent.

nonEmpty.description: The path resolves to a value that is not null, "", [] or {}.

isList.description: The path resolves to a list, or does not resolve at all. An empty list satisfies it, and so does an absent one: a single-page List* legally returns an empty page, and some AWS services omit that member entirely instead of serializing []. A present value that is not a list fails it.

equals.description: The path resolves to a value equal (as JSON) to the evaluated expression.

matches.description: The path resolves to a string matching this RE2-compatible regular expression.

missing.description: The path does not resolve (any segment absent).

Where.description: Item-relative path → expected value. An item matches when every entry is equal. `$` is the item itself.

code.description: The wire error code: the awsQueryError code where declared, else the shape name. An interpreter accepts an error whose SDK-reported code or type name equals either.

Path.description: A response path: `$`, then any number of `.Member` or `[index]` segments. Not JSONPath.

Value.description: A value expression: an expression object with exactly one $-key, or structural JSON whose leaves are values.

oneOf.description: A blob: canonical standard base64 text, or a $ref to a blob a previous call exported. The only value a blob member takes (compat/model/README.md § Values).

The client's clock at the moment the call is made, in epoch milliseconds, plus offsetMillis. Read once per call, so every $now in one call's params sees the same instant. Only for a long member, and never on the expected side of a check (compat/model/README.md § Values).

offsetMillis.description: Added to the instant; omitted rather than 0, so each value has one spelling.
